# Trim

> A free, open-source tool that debloats Windows 10 and 11. It removes
> advertising, telemetry and preinstalled apps, tunes what is left for games,
> shows every change before making it, and writes a script that undoes them all.

Run it with one line in PowerShell:

    irm https://trimbloat.com/go | iex

## What it does

- Removes advertising ID, telemetry, suggested content, Copilot, Widgets, Bing
  in search, Start menu recommendations, and preinstalled apps.
- Tunes for gaming: Game Bar and background capture off, windowed-game
  optimisations on, CPU priority favouring the foreground, and installed games
  pointed at the high-performance GPU.
- Disk cleanup across every drive: 14 categories, each itemised with its size
  and location before anything is deleted.
- Deep uninstall: runs an app's own uninstaller, then finds and offers the
  folders, registry keys, services and scheduled tasks it left behind.

## What makes it different

- Nothing is changed until the user clicks Apply. A dry run needs no
  administrator rights and prints the entire plan.
- Every change is labelled SAFE, CAUTION or RISKY. Only SAFE is selected by
  default.
- Every registry write is recorded before it is made, and the run emits a
  standalone rollback script at C:\ProgramData\Trim\undo. A System Restore
  point is taken first.
- Hardware is detected, so laptop/desktop and NVIDIA/AMD/Intel differences are
  respected rather than guessed at.
- The build is reproducible: cloning the source and compiling it produces
  byte-identical output to the published script, whose SHA256 is at /sha256.

## What it deliberately will not do

- Touch the camera, microphone, screenshots or screen recording.
- Change fan curves, BIOS settings, or apply any overclock.
- Configure AutoLogon, which writes the account password to the registry.
- Remove load-bearing components: shared frameworks, winget, Xbox sign-in.

## Attribution

The debloat and tweak engine is WinUtil by Chris Titus Tech
(https://github.com/ChrisTitusTech/winutil), invoked by Trim rather than
reimplemented. Trim adds the reversible wrapper around it.
